jobs.title: Director, Project Governance
jobs.description:
Job Description

What if you could redefine what’s possible?

With us, you can. You want Purpose. Growth. Opportunity.
People who get it.

We are the home of ambitious, passionate, and innovative world shapers.

With an unmatched breadth and depth of engineering, advisory and science‑based expertise, our global minds unite to power local solutions.

We are pathfinders and impact makers.

We are Visioneers.

We are WSP.

The Opportunity

Successful projects don't happen by accident. They are delivered through strong governance, disciplined execution, effective project controls, and leaders who give teams the tools and support they need to succeed.

WSP is seeking an experienced and passionate project delivery leader to join our Earth & Environment team as Director, Project Governance, BC & Yukon. This is a unique opportunity
to shape and lead the project management function across one of WSP's largest and most diverse regions. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Earth & Environment, BC & Yukon, you will establish and drive a regional project governance and project management office (PMO)
approach that strengthens consistency, accountability, and delivery performance across a diverse portfolio of environmental engineering projects.

As the leader responsible for project governance, project controls and project management capability, you will oversee our Project Controllers and Project Control Administrators while building the systems, processes, tools and performance rhythms that enable successful project delivery. You will work closely with operational leaders and project teams to improve project outcomes, strengthen commercial performance, enhance project management capability and create a more predictable and disciplined approach to delivering work.

This role is ideal for someone energized by project management excellence
, governance, continuous improvement and helping others succeed. If you are passionate about creating the frameworks, insights and support systems that allow teams to consistently deliver successful outcomes for clients and the business, we would love to hear from you.

Your Impact

Establish and lead a consistent project governance and controls framework across the BC & Yukon Earth & Environment business, strengthening accountability, discipline and delivery excellence.
Drive adoption of project management standards, tools and best practices to improve project execution, predictability, commercial performance and client outcomes.
Provide oversight of portfolio health, using performance insights to identify risks, trends and opportunities, and lead reviews or recovery efforts for strategic, high-risk or underperforming projects.
Lead and develop Project Controllers and Project Control Administrators, aligning resources and capabilities to provide effective support across the regional portfolio.
Build project management capability through practical tools, training, coaching and knowledge sharing, while serving as a trusted advisor to leaders and project teams.
Strengthen forecasting, risk management, change management and commercial practices to improve profitability and reduce delivery risk.
Partner with operations, finance, commercial, risk and legal teams to align project delivery with regional and national priorities.
Lead continuous improvement and lessons learned initiatives, and support strategic pursuits, business planning and key initiatives by ensuring project readiness, governance and delivery risks are effectively considered.

The Skills That Set You Apart

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Project Management, Business, Environmental Sciences, or a related discipline.
Professional certification or designation such as PMP, PgMP, PRINCE2 Practitioner or equivalent project governance, risk, or program management credentials considered an asset.
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in project management, project controls, program oversight, governance, or professional consulting environments.
Proven experience overseeing complex, multidisciplinary project portfolios and supporting successful project delivery across diverse stakeholder groups.
Strong understanding of project management methodologies, governance frameworks, project controls, commercial management, and performance reporting.
Demonstrated success leading organizational change, continuous improvement, and capability-building initiatives.
Experience identifying and managing financial, operational, contractual, regulatory, and project delivery risks.
Strong business acumen, financial literacy, and an ability to translate project performance data into actionable business insights.
Experience working with enterprise project and financial management systems, such as Oracle, to support governance, forecasting, and decision-making.
Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage effectively with executives, operational leaders, project sponsors, and project teams.
A collaborative leadership style with a proven ability to influence, drive accountability, and achieve results in a matrixed environment without direct authority.
A passion for project delivery excellence, continuous improvement, and helping project teams achieve successful outcomes for clients and the business.

Why Choose WSP?

We exist to shape communities to advance humanity. The brightest engineers, advisors and scientists from across the globe call WSP home.

Proudly Canadian – we are a Top 100 Employer in Canada for 2026.
A global community of brilliant minds – your next idea, mentor, or opportunity is always within reach.
Limitless opportunities start here. Whether it’s across the country or around the globe, we help you tailor your role to match your ambition — because your growth drives ours.
Flexible work, real balance – we recognize the importance of balance in our lives and encourage you to prioritize the balance in yours.

#WeAreWSP

Compensation

AB, BC, NT, NU, SK & YT:
$177,000 - $234,000

MB & ON:
$161,500 - $222,300

NB, NL, NS, PE & QC:
$$159,900 - $212,300

Disclosure:

The final salary awarded for this role may vary from the above range based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs. The wage range provided in this job posting may be subject to change for business purposes.

Explore Limitless Possibilities

If you are passionate about project governance, delivery excellence and building high-performing project management functions, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact. You will have the platform to influence how projects are delivered, strengthen capability across the business, and help shape a culture of accountability, continuous improvement and project excellence.

About Us

At WSP
, we exist to shape communities to advance humanity.

It’s why we bring people together who are wired to solve complex challenges - engineers, scientists, advisors, and technical experts who are driven by a common passion - to redefine what’s possible and shape what comes next. We are Visioneers.

As one of the world’s leading professional services firms, we partner with clients across transportation, infrastructure, environment, buildings, energy, water, mining and metals. We pair deep local knowledge with global insights to pioneer solutions designed to leave a lasting, positive impact.

At WSP
, you’ll join a community of brilliant minds that push boundaries every day - applying deep expertise and fuelling innovation to help create a more connected and resilient future. Here, your ideas are valued, your growth is supported, and you are encouraged to bring your authentic self to work. We empower our people to collaborate across disciplines, challenge the status quo, and shape a career with purpose.

Join us.

Please Note:

Health and Safety is a core paramount value of WSP. Given the importance of keeping one another safe it is expected that you comply with our Health, Safety & Environment (HSE) policy at all times as well as client HSE policies when working at client locations. Full details here .

Some safety-sensitive positions involve fieldwork and may include work in a variety of environmental conditions, such as remote or isolated areas, working alone, and in inclement weather (within safe and reasonable limits).

WSP welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

WSP is committed to the principles of employment equity. Only the candidates selected will be contacted.

WSP does not accept unsolicited resumes from agencies. Full details here .

jobs.title: Director Planning & Performance
jobs.description:
JOIN OUR TEAM

Metro Supply Chain
is a strategic supply chain solutions partner to some of the world's fastest growing and most reputable organizations. For 50 years, it has excelled at tailoring integrated, data driven solutions, fueled by advanced systems and technology, that fulfill complex and challenging distribution needs. Managing 22.5 million square feet operating out of more than 190 sites across North America and Europe with a team of 9,000, it is one of Canada's largest privately owned supply chain solutions companies. Metro Supply Chain is a 2026 winner of the Canada's Best Managed Companies program, recognized for its strategic expertise, culture of innovation and commitment to its people and local communities.

Drive Growth. Shape Strategy. Influence Big Decisions.

We are seeking a strategic and commercially minded Director Planning & Performance
to lead pricing governance, deal economics, customer profitability, and commercial financial analysis across our growing business. This is a high-impact leadership role that partners closely with Business Development, Operations, Legal, FP&A, revenue assurance and executive leaders to support profitable growth and informed decision-making.

If you're equally comfortable building sophisticated financial models, influencing senior leaders, and crafting compelling business cases that drive action, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Lead Pricing Strategy & Deal Economics

Evaluate and structure financial models for new business opportunities, contract renewals, expansions, and strategic customer initiatives.
Develop pricing models, cost-to-serve analyses, margin requirements, and commercial governance processes.
Assess profitability drivers across warehousing, transportation, fulfillment, and broader supply chain solutions.
Support negotiations and executive approval processes with data-driven recommendations and financial insights.

Develop Business Cases & Executive-Level Insights

Build robust financial models and scenario analyses to support strategic decisions.
Translate complex data into clear, compelling presentations and recommendations for senior leadership.
Partner with cross-functional teams to assess opportunities, investments, and operational improvements.
Ensure analytical integrity, model accuracy, and strong governance practices.

Drive Profitability & Performance

Lead customer, contract, site, and service-line profitability analysis.
Identify opportunities to improve margins, pricing effectiveness, and operational performance.
Conduct post-deal reviews to measure actual performance against business case assumptions.
Develop KPI dashboards and commercial performance reporting that support continuous improvement.

Partner with the Business

Act as a trusted finance partner to Business Development and Operations teams from opportunity identification through implementation.
Evaluate contract terms, risk exposure, service commitments, and investment requirements.
Facilitate cross-functional collaboration and guide stakeholders toward commercially sound decisions.
Help strengthen commercial finance capabilities, processes, and best practices across the organization.

What you will bring?

Education & Credentials

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, Supply Chain, or a related field.
CPA, MBA, or other advanced financial designation preferred.

Experience

8-10 years of progressive experience in Commercial Finance, FP&A, Pricing, Deal Advisory, or Business Performance Management.
5+ years leading complex projects, cross-functional teams, pricing initiatives, or commercial finance activities.
Experience within third-party logistics (3PL), supply chain, transportation, warehousing, distribution, or fulfillment environments is strongly preferred.

At Metro Supply Chain, you'll play a critical role in shaping the financial success of customer partnerships and strategic growth initiatives. You'll have direct exposure to executive leadership, influence major commercial decisions, and help drive profitable growth across one of Canada's leading supply chain organizations.

If you're looking for an opportunity to combine financial expertise, commercial strategy, and business leadership, we encourage you to apply.

Why Join Us

Work in an environment where safety is our first priority
The opportunity to build a career with a growing company
Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family
Life and disability insurance
Wellness programs to support your family’s well-being
A Retirement Savings Program with a company match
Company team wear allowance
Employee Appreciation Day
Company sponsored social events
Community volunteering

We are an equal opportunity employer
committed to building and fostering a diverse workplace where people feel included and valued. We encourage applications from all qualified individuals. Should you require accommodation for a special ability or need during the recruitment process, please reach out to a member of our Human Resources Team.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
Job Purpose

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization.

The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement.

Key Duties And Responsibilities

AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management

Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals.
Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness.
Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options.
Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes.
Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks.

AI Solution Development & Implementation

Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities.
Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working.
Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement.
Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured.
Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk.

AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption

Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption.
Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks.
Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements.
Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed.
Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required.

Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management

Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users.
Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI.
Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support.
Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement.
Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption

Vendor, Technology & Partner Management

Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership.
Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization.
Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation.
Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value.

Qualifications, Skills, And Educational Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption.
Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization.
Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI.
Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.
Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS

Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office)
Fast paced office environment
Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

jobs.title: Director, Information Technology
jobs.description:
Company Description

Alberta Beverage Container Recycling Corporation (ABCRC) manages the deposit-return system for non-refillable beverage containers sold in Alberta, supporting an efficient and reliable recycling infrastructure across the province. Since 1995, ABCRC has recycled more than 42 billion beverage containers through a network of 220+ independently owned Alberta depots. ABCRC team members contribute to environmental sustainability, circular economy initiatives, and responsible environmental stewardship through beverage container recycling. More information is available at https://www.abcrc.com.

Role Description

This newly created, strategic leadership role will define how technology enables the business. As Director, Information technology (IT), you will own enterprise systems, cloud infrastructure, Microsoft 365, identity and access management, IT service management and IT governance, building a secure, scalable and high-performing technology environment that supports business growth and operational excellence.

What You'll Do

Set the direction for enterprise technology strategy, governance, and modernization.
Strengthen security, resilience, and service performance across core platforms.
Define the AI adoption strategy and governance guardrails, measure productivity results, and ensure AI does not introduce unnecessary security or operational risk.

More Detail

Enterprise Systems Leadership
Own the strategy, roadmap, performance, and improvement of enterprise systems, company websites, and portals.
Partner with business leaders to improve processes, controls, and reporting.
Lead prioritization, integration, data quality, and automation to deliver reliable, scalable information.

Cloud, Infrastructure & Modern Workplace 
Lead cloud, infrastructure, and modern workplace strategy across Azure, Microsoft 365, identity, networking, endpoints, and collaboration tools.
Ensure high availability, resilience, scalability, and cost-effective platform performance.
Oversee identity and access management, including SSO, MFA, privileged access, and lifecycle governance.
Modernize legacy technologies and maintain a secure, well-governed workplace.

IT Service Management  

Establish and mature IT service management (ITSM) capabilities across incident, problem, change, request, asset, and service catalog management.
Improve service delivery and user experience through SLAs, metrics, and continuous improvement.
Provide dashboards and reporting on service performance, operational health, and business impact.

Cybersecurity, Risk & Resilience 
Own cybersecurity strategy, governance, and execution across identity, endpoint, cloud, network, and third-party risk.
Strengthen security through modern controls, awareness, monitoring, and incident response.
Lead business continuity, disaster recovery, and cyber resilience planning.
Ensure technology risks are identified, communicated, and managed.

IT Policy, Standards & Governance 
Establish and maintain IT policies, standards, and control frameworks across infrastructure, security, identity and access, data retention, and operations.
Ensure policies are practical, auditable, and aligned with business, legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements.
Drive governance that improves technology decisions, architectural consistency, and control maturity.
Govern cost allocation and chargeback models that enable clarity, fairness, and strong business partner relationships.
Manage strategic vendors and partners, including website and portal service providers, to maximize delivery quality, resilience, and value.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, information systems, or a related field.
7+ years of progressive IT experience, including 5+ years in senior leadership with accountability for enterprise-wide technology strategy and budgets.
Track record leading enterprise systems, data governance, reporting platforms, and service delivery.
Deep expertise in Microsoft technologies (Azure, Microsoft 365, and Entra ID), including backup and data retention.
Strong background in cybersecurity leadership and operations, including incident response, vulnerability management, network security, and third-party risk.
Experience with IT controls, audit readiness, regulatory compliance, and policy governance.
Vendor management expertise, including directing vendor-managed or outsourced IT environments.
Proven success in cloud transformation, infrastructure modernization, and technology standardization.
Demonstrated financial acumen, including IT budget development, capital planning, cost optimization and value realization.
Exceptional leadership and business partnering skills.

Nice to Have

Graduate degree and/or relevant industry certifications.
Strong background in reporting, analytics, automation, and systems integration.
Hands-on familiarity with VMware, backup and data retention software, and Cisco (or equivalent) firewalls, VPN, and switching.
Experience introducing AI technologies into business operations, including driving adoption and governing risk.
Experience establishing and maturing ITSM operating models.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Ontario Plants Propagation (OP) is a leading North American plant propagation company focused on producing high-quality young vegetable and soft fruit plants for commercial greenhouse growers. As a critical supplier to the controlled environment agriculture sector, OP combines horticultural expertise, advanced growing capabilities, and a commitment to innovation to support a more resilient, productive, and sustainable food system.

Following the development of its state-of-the-art Glencoe greenhouse facility and significant capital investment, OP is entering an exciting next phase of growth and transformation. The organization is focused on optimizing operations, enhancing profitability, expanding capabilities, and strengthening its position in a market benefiting from growing demand for greenhouse-grown food production.

The Mandate

Reporting directly to the CEO and working closely with ownership, the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) will play a central role in helping build a high-performing, scalable, and profitable organization. This is not a traditional finance leadership position focused solely on stewardship and reporting. It is an opportunity to become a true business partner and strategic leader, influencing critical decisions that will shape the future of the company.

The successful candidate will join at a pivotal point in OP's evolution. With substantial investments already made in infrastructure and growth, the organization is seeking a finance leader who can help unlock value by improving profitability, strengthening cash generation, enhancing decision-making capabilities, and building the financial and operational foundations needed to support long-term success.

For an executive who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, building capabilities, and creating lasting impact, this role offers a rare opportunity to influence strategy, strengthen culture, enhance performance, and leave a visible mark on a growing business.

Leadership and Stewardship

The company is seeking a CFO who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. More than just a technical financial leader, the successful candidate will be a thoughtful and credible executive who fosters trust, accountability, and collaboration across the organization and partners effectively with external stakeholders.
Operationally curious and highly intelligent, with a low-ego leadership style
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and complexity
A builder of high-performing teams and organizational culture
Results-oriented and accountable
An enabler of exceptional data-driven decision making
Collaborative, trusted, and relationship-focused
Energized by operational challenges and continuous improvement
An effective and transparent communicator

Ideal Background

The successful candidate will be a strategic and operational finance executive who enjoys complexity and thrives in a growth-oriented environment. They will bring both financial expertise and a passion for helping businesses improve performance and create value.
CPA designation required.
Proven track record of success as a CFO or senior finance executive within a complex operating environment with a minimum of 15 years, including optimizing and scaling organizations
Accomplished as a strategic business partner, advisor to the CEO and the senior leadership team
Hands-on and strategic capabilities in financial planning, forecasting, cash flow management, and business intelligence, driving operational improvements through financial insights and performance management.
Experience operating in asset-intensive, capital-intensive, or leveraged environments.
Track record of building high-performing teams and influencing leaders across an organization.
Experience in manufacturing, food production, agriculture, horticulture, or other operationally intensive industries is strongly preferred.
Experience working with sophisticated lenders, private equity sponsors, family offices, or institutional investors is also an asset.

Location

The CFO will maintain a meaningful on-site presence and build strong relationships across both operating locations. Regular travel between St. Thomas and Glencoe is expected as part of developing a deep understanding of the business and supporting operational excellence.

Why This Role

This is an opportunity to join an organization at a defining moment in its journey. Significant investments have been made, the platform for growth is in place, and the leadership team is focused on realizing the full potential of the business. For a finance executive who wants to influence strategy, strengthen operations, develop teams, and help create long-term enterprise value, this role offers both challenge and impact.

If you are energized by building, improving, and leading from the front, we welcome the opportunity to connect.
